verdicts.note: Matching-model theory of monogamy versus polygyny; 'household formation' is the modelling frame.
No abstract; family structure and wellbeing at OLDER ages in Japan.
Clinical protocol for psychological intervention in infertility; young people leaving home later appears in the framing sentence only.

Early-life debt -- college loans and credit card balances -- against HOMEOWNERSHIP, MARRIAGE AND FERTILITY after leaving college, Survey of Consumer Finances. C.3.g owns the treatment, but it estimates the household-formation chain through to a birth in one dataset, which is the structure this chapter is short of. Report to C.3.g and read.
Single mothers by choice.
Toilet training in a Brazilian birth cohort.
Social networks and longevity among the Chinese elderly.
Elderly grandmothers caring for AIDS orphans in South Africa; the three-generation household with the dependency running to the children.
No abstract; preprint duplicate of the Handbook chapter on household formation and rural marriage markets.
Omnibus review of books on Japanese population decline and ageing.
Book review, ritual and sexual values in Tokugawa Japan.
Chapter on contact frequency between parents and adult children.
Reference entry titled 'Family Formation' with no abstract.
Introduction to a volume on European demographic change.
Geographical proximity between parents and adult children as an indicator of solidarity. Proximity as exposure, support as outcome -- adjacent to PRIMARY_PROXIMITY but without a fertility outcome.
Nineteenth-century intergenerational co-residence in the Sundsvall region; whether industrialisation changed it. Historical, and the dependency runs to the old.
No abstract; dynamic microsimulation methods chapter.
Comparative introduction to ageing societies.
Plasmid replicon typing; 'F fertility' is the bacterial sense.
No abstract; shifting parenthood to advanced reproductive ages. A.15's.
No abstract; stepparenting and mental health.
No abstract; 'Living Arrangements, Health and Well-Being' names the exposure but an outcome that is not fertility.
Cultural-studies essay on the American staycation.

Giuliano's cultural-norms and family-formation chapter: in Italy, Portugal, Greece and Spain 70-80% of 18-33 year olds live at home, alongside rising age at marriage and declining fertility. The registered hypothesis's central stylised fact with a cultural-transmission mechanism attached. Priority read -- Giuliano's identification strategy elsewhere uses second-generation immigrants, which is a route to within-setting variation that scope §4 did not enumerate.
Comparative study of Chinese families in Taiwan and southeast China. Context for the extended arm; preprint of the OUP book also in this batch.
Reproductive contributions of foreign wives in Taiwan by source country.
Welfare policy design and single parenthood in Canada versus the US.

AGE AT FIRST REPRODUCTION under differing KINSHIP ECOLOGIES, where residence and descent rules channel resources to women. An arrangement-system exposure with a fertility-timing outcome; identification is systemic rather than within-setting.
Book review, Japanese population decline and the labour market.
No abstract; Taiwanese minor marriage and inbreeding avoidance -- co-residence in the Westermarck sense, a different construct.
No abstract; household division of labour and cross-country differences in HOUSEHOLD FORMATION RATES. A theory of link 1's cross-country variation, which is the pattern the pre-launch arm rests on.
Timing of parenthood relative to other transitions and adult social functioning.

CO-RESIDENCE WITH ADULT CHILDREN as an 'off-time' parental role against parents' mental health in late midlife. The parents' side of the pre-launch arrangement, with wellbeing rather than fertility as the outcome -- the same framing as the Japanese cost-to-parents chapter.
No abstract; geographic proximity in four-generation families. Adjacent to PRIMARY_PROXIMITY.

JEEA published version of the mortgage-cost paper seen as an SSRN preprint in batch 9. Estimates the impact of the COST OF A MORTGAGE on the probability of leaving the parental home, explicitly motivated by the implications for FERTILITY, and explains the North-South European gradient the pre-launch arm rests on. Wall 1's mixed case with an identified design: the treatment is a price, the target is the arrangement. Priority read, and it belongs in the Wall 1 second-read packet with Aparicio-Fenoll. Duplicate pair with W1529588091 -- keep this published version.
Timing of family transitions in West Germany from GSOEP, testing destandardisation and individualisation. Panel data covering the sequence.
Elderly suicide rates against household size and the share of EXTENDED HOUSEHOLDS across countries. Arrangement as exposure, suicide as outcome.
Grandchild-grandparent contact across early adulthood.

'Families as Roommates': a theory of household size in which living arrangements are chosen, tracking the US decline from 1850 to 2000. The economic model of link 1, and the framing that makes co-residence a choice rather than a constraint -- which is §3's problem stated as a modelling assumption.
No abstract; preprint of the Japanese 'parasite singles' paper below.
Sole versus partnered parents' psychiatric illness, with CO-RESIDENCE WITH OTHER ADULTS as a proxy for support. Arrangement as a covariate, mental illness as outcome.
Poverty and critical events in emerging adulthood; the lengthened transition among vulnerable subgroups.
Living arrangements of young adults in BRAZIL, set against postponement of marriage and fertility. Latin American setting, which the frame is thin on.
Determinants of elderly living arrangements in Orissa.
Loneliness among older adults in Russia and Bulgaria.
Demographic transition and women's status in Taiwan, framed around the patriarchal, patrilineal and PATRILOCAL family. Context for the extended arm; no estimate.

No abstract, but the title 'Co-residence and Family Size' names both axes exactly. An OUP chapter that must be traced -- this is the shape of a primary-cell record and the screen cannot see which configuration.
Book version of Understanding Chinese Families; duplicate of the RePEc preprint above.
ERP study of morphological decomposition; 'family size' is the lexical statistic. A clean homonym on the outcome axis.
Book review, age and old age in late Victorian Canada and the US.
Multi-state household projection for car-fleet forecasting in Belo Horizonte.

Japan's 'parasite singles': the rise in UNMARRIED ADULTS LIVING WITH THEIR PARENTS, framed against the fertility decline but with the household economy and income inequality as the estimated outcome. The exposure is exactly the pre-launch arrangement; the outcome is not a birth.
Cohabitation versus marriage in the NLSY79, with fertility patterns. A.7's.
OECD review of Slovenian social policy.
Chapter on changing family practices and relationships.
